reuse.why: Fintegra reuses the SimpleFIN link path and the Akahu download is generalised into downloadProviderTransactions, but taking over a link rewrites unlinkAccount's field reset inline instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Six near-identical per-provider assert*AccountIsNotLinked closures and six near-identical app.method lambdas, the closed-account check called in each link function and again inside the duplicate-link assertion, and a copy of unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount field list.

placement.why: Link preconditions sit in accounts/app.ts at registration and the download helper in sync.ts, which fits the tree, but Fintegra is folded into a function still named linkSimpleFinAccount and the closed check is split between the registration lambdas' helper and each link body.

scope.why: Edits stay on the four requested behaviours plus tests; the Akahu download refactor is in service of the Fintegra step.

maintainability.why: The provider-specific wrapper boilerplate grows by two edits per new provider, linkSimpleFinAccount now carries a source parameter and an orgDomain type-guard for another provider, and the closed rule is checked in two places by design.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountIsNotLinked unlinks the previous holder with its own db.updateAccount field reset instead of the existing unlinkAccount logic (accounts/app.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: The six assert<Provider>AccountIsNotLinked closures and six app.method lambdas repeat the same call with only the provider/field renamed instead of one wrapper taking the provider; the unlink field reset is copied from unlinkAccount.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountIsNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink with a replace branch that also re-runs the closed check; linkSimpleFinAccount gains a `source` parameter and an `'orgDomain' in externalAccount` special case for Fintegra; the replace branch bypasses unlinkAccount.
